title: Structural induction for Boolean circuits
statement: Let $P$ be a property of Boolean circuit trees on $n$ variables. Suppose $P$ holds for every literal circuit, and that for every choice of gate type and list of child circuits, if $P$ holds for each child in the list, then it holds for the circuit formed by that gate and list. Then $P$ holds for every Boolean circuit tree on $n$ variables.
hypotheses_covered: For every gate type and child list, $P$ for each listed child implies $P$ for the resulting node circuit
replaced:
Let $P$ be a property of Boolean circuits on $n$ variables. Suppose that $P$ holds for
every literal circuit, and that whenever $P$ holds for every circuit in a list $cs$ of
children, it also holds for the gate circuit $\mathrm{node}(isAnd, cs)$ formed from $cs$
(an AND gate when $isAnd = \mathrm{true}$, an OR gate when $isAnd = \mathrm{false}$).
Then $P$ holds for every Boolean circuit on $n$ variables.
